blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Demand forecasting in practice is a blend of data and judgement. The data tells you what happened; the judgement tells you what it means. Neither works alone. A spreadsheet full of perfect history can still be wrong if nobody notices that a major customer is switching supplier, and the best-informed gut is still dangerous if it is not disciplined by the numbers.

The intermediate forecaster uses three inputs together: historical patterns such as seasonality, trend and baseline; quantitative signals such as recent sales, promotions and competitor activity; and qualitative input — what the sales team is hearing from customers and what the supplier is saying about delivery.

Crucially, the good forecaster admits uncertainty. Saying "it might rise by 5 to 10%" is more honest, and more useful, than saying "7% exactly" when you know perfectly well that the truth could be either side of that.

items.q: According to the text, what is demand forecasting in practice?
options: A blend of data and judgement
items.why: "Demand forecasting in practice is a blend of data and judgement."

items.q: Which three inputs does the intermediate forecaster combine?
options: Historical patterns, quantitative signals and qualitative input
items.why: "three inputs together: historical patterns… quantitative signals… and qualitative input."

items.q: Why is a perfect spreadsheet of history still described as potentially wrong?
options: Because judgement is more accurate than data
Because the maths may contain errors
Because it can miss real-world changes, like a customer switching supplier
Because it is always out of date
items.why: "can still be wrong if nobody notices that a major customer is switching supplier."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Admitting uncertainty can be more useful than false precision.
The sales team is a valuable source of qualitative input.
Data and judgement should reinforce each other.
A single precise number is the most professional forecast.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que uma faixa honesta vale mais que um número exato falso, como "7% exactly".

items.q: What does "the best-informed gut is still dangerous" suggest about intuition?
options: Intuition is more reliable than data
Only senior planners should trust their intuition
Intuition is safe only when checked against the numbers
items.why: Inferência: "dangerous if it is not disciplined by the numbers" — a intuição precisa ser checada pelos dados.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie orientando uma planejadora. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, let's look at your forecast for the next quarter. You've written a single number — 12,000 units. It's a clean number, and I understand why it feels professional. But let me push you a little.

Where did the 12,000 come from? You checked the seasonality, you looked at last month's sales, and you factored in the spring promotion. That's good work. But have you spoken to the sales team this week? Because if one of them tells me a big account might reduce its order, then 12,000 could be optimistic.

Here's what I'd like you to do instead. Give operations a range. Say demand may land between 11,000 and 13,500, and tell them where the risk sits. That way they can plan the buffer stock properly.

A single number looks confident, but it hides the uncertainty. Operations would rather know the truth than trust a figure that could be wrong by two thousand units. Honesty about the range is not a weakness — it's the whole job.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the planner's forecast written as?
items.why: "You've written a single number — 12,000 units."

items.q: Which inputs did the planner already use?
options: The buffer stock levels from operations
Seasonality, last month's sales and the spring promotion
items.why: "you checked the seasonality, you looked at last month's sales, and you factored in the spring promotion."

items.q: What does Sophie say the planner has NOT yet done?
options: Spoken to the sales team this week
items.why: "have you spoken to the sales team this week?" — a etapa qualitativa que faltou.

items.q: Why does Sophie prefer a range for operations?
options: Because it always looks more confident
Because it lets them plan the buffer stock properly
Because it avoids talking to the sales team
Because it is faster to calculate
items.why: Inferência: "Give operations a range… That way they can plan the buffer stock properly."

items.q: What does Sophie imply about a single confident number?
options: It should always be rounded up
It can hide uncertainty and mislead operations
It is fine as long as it comes from data
It is the mark of an experienced planner
items.why: Inferência: "looks confident, but it hides the uncertainty" — parece seguro, mas engana quem planeja.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A good forecast is a blend of numbers and market feel." A blend is…
options: a mixture of things combined together
items.why: Blend = mistura: elementos combinados que trabalham juntos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Ice-cream sales show strong ___, peaking every summer."
items.why: Seasonality = sazonalidade: o padrão que se repete em certas épocas do ano.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Strip out the promotions and the summer spike, and the ___ demand is about 8,000 units a month."
items.why: Baseline = linha base: o nível de fundo, sem picos nem promoções.

items.q: "We rely on both quantitative and qualitative inputs." Quantitative input is…
options: based on numbers and measurable data
items.why: Quantitative = quantitativo: baseado em números e dados mensuráveis.

items.q: "A forecast that admits uncertainty is more honest than a fixed number." Uncertainty is…
options: the state of not knowing something exactly
items.why: Uncertainty = incerteza: não saber o resultado exato de antemão.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de planejamento. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The planning lead has to sign off on the final forecast." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Operations pushed back on the optimistic estimate." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Let's factor in the spring promotion before we finalise the numbers." To factor in means to…
items.why: Factor in = levar em conta, incluir no cálculo.

items.q: "A tighter range won't move the needle unless we talk to customers." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível no resultado.

items.q: "New orders came in, so we had to revise the forecast upwards." To revise upwards means to…
items.why: Revise upwards = revisar para cima, aumentar a estimativa.
